value.overview: The Violet-crowned Hummingbird (Ramosomyia violiceps) is a hummingbird recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from white underparts, green upperparts, straight red bill with dark tip, and violet-blue crown in males. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 2 state or DC summaries, including AZ, NM. It is most associated with Forests:  Tropical Dry, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Violet-crowned Hummingbird belongs to the family Hummingbirds in the order Apodiformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for white underparts, green upperparts, straight red bill with dark tip, and violet-blue crown in males. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.

value.dietFeeding: It feeds mainly on nectar from tubular flowers and also takes tiny insects and spiders for protein. It often hovers at flowers, visits flowering shrubs or trees, and may defend good nectar sources from other hummingbirds.
value.behavior: It is quick, alert, and often territorial around good flowers or feeders. Males may use display flights, while both sexes make fast direct flights between feeding and resting perches.
